problem: Many simulators exist for embodied AI (AI2-THOR, Gibson, MINOS, Habitat), but there has been no open, reproducible way to test whether policies trained in simulation work on a real robot. Real-world testing is expensive and interactive, it needs tightly aligned sim and real worlds, and physical conditions are hard to repeat.
motivation: Shared ecosystems like ImageNet and COCO drove progress in visual recognition. Embodied AI lacks an equivalent standardized, affordable sim-to-real benchmark, so only well-resourced labs can study real-world transfer. The authors observe that sim and real images look alike to humans but separate clearly in deep feature space, and that real control dynamics differ from simulation. This suggests the sim-to-real gap is large and poorly understood.
key_idea: Build RoboTHOR: modular, artist-designed simulated apartments (on AI2-THOR), some with carefully matched, reconfigurable physical replicas driven by a LoCoBot through a platform-agnostic API and remote HTTP access, then benchmark object-goal (semantic) navigation both sim-to-sim and sim-to-real.
insight: Visual similarity to the human eye does not mean feature-space similarity. t-SNE of ResNet-18 features on 846 paired sim/real images forms separate real and sim clusters. A COCO Faster-RCNN scores mAP 0.338 on real vs 0.255 on sim images. Both help explain why an RGB A3C policy's success and especially SPL collapse on the real robot (easy SR 55.30→33.33, SPL 38.12→3.53). Even a policy overfit to the test-dev scene in simulation (SR 100, SPL 82.17 easy) keeps SR on the robot for easy starts but drops sharply in SPL (12.28) and loses success on hard starts (94.12→50). Changing the camera FOV between training (90°) and test (42.5°) cuts real-world success to 16% on easy and 0% on medium/hard, with the robot rotating endlessly. CycleGAN real→sim translation gives 0% success. Together these show that frozen internet-pretrained representations and naive image translation are brittle across domains.
method: Scene corpus: 89 artist-built apartments (60 train / 15 val in sim only; 4 test-dev and 10 test-standard with physical counterparts) drawn from 15/2/5 wall layouts, with no overlap in wall layouts or object instances across splits.

Modular asset library: 731 unique object instances, 11 furniture types and 32 small-object types, mostly real IKEA items. 14 small-object categories are designated navigation targets present in every scene.

Physical space: an 8.8m×3.9m area with lightweight ProPanel walls, reconfigurable to a new apartment in about 30 minutes, costing about $10k and designed to be replicable. Super-NIA-3D localization is used only for evaluation and visualization.

Agent & API: LoCoBot with Intel RealSense RGB-D, replicated in simulation with matching camera. A platform-agnostic API is built on PyRobot, with remote HTTP access and a scheduler. Gaussian actuation noise is added in simulation (translation mean 0.001m, std 0.005m; rotation std 0.5°), with parameters estimated from manual measurements.

Task: visual semantic navigation to a named object category. Full action set is MoveAhead/RotateLeft/RotateRight/LookUp/LookDown/Done. Success requires the object in view, within a distance threshold, and Done called. Humans need a median of 49.5 steps vs 22.0 for shortest paths.

Baselines: Random, Instant Done, Blind (LSTM with only the target embedding). Image-A3C: frozen ResNet-18 7×7×512 features → two 1×1 convs to 32 channels, concatenated with a 64-d target embedding → LSTM, trained with A3C (+5 success reward, −0.01 step penalty). Image+Detection-A3C adds COCO Faster-RCNN detections embedded into a 7×7×120 grid (top 3 boxes per cell).
Sim2real analyses: t-SNE of ResNet features, cross-domain detector mAP, camera FOV mismatch, and CycleGAN real→sim image translation.

setting.backbone: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 (frozen) + conv/LSTM actor-critic policy trained from scratch with A3C; optional MS-COCO Faster-RCNN detector (frozen)
setting.training_data: RoboTHOR simulation only: 50 of the training scenes, 100,000 A3C episodes (32 threads, 8 TITAN X), single target category (Television), random scene and start per episode. The overfit variant is trained on a single test-dev scene.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (plus a target word embedding); the platform also supports depth
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead, RotateLeft 45°, RotateRight 45°, Done (with Gaussian actuation noise in sim); the full task definition also includes LookUp/LookDown
setting.simulator: RoboTHOR (built on AI2-THOR / Unity) + physical replica apartments
setting.privileged: none (Super-NIA-3D localization used only for evaluation/visualization; the overfit variant is trained on the test-dev scene itself)

numbers_note: The paper is a platform/benchmark paper, so the 'own methods' are the A3C baselines. Results are split by Easy/Medium/Hard start difficulty; no overall aggregate is reported. Table 3 also has an 'Image Sim-2-Sim' overfit row (Easy 100/82.17/8.09/1.05; Medium 100/86.17/27.52/4.77; Hard 94.12/83.18/42.26/7.90), summarized in the 4th entry's extra field. Text-only results: the FOV-mismatch experiment (train 90°, test 42.5°) gives real-world success of 16% easy and 0% medium/hard; CycleGAN real→sim translation gives 0% on the remaining test-dev scene. The split word 'test' is used for the paper's 'test-dev' scenes, which it describes as used for real-world validation. Trivial baselines (Random 7.58 SR easy, Instant Done/Blind 4.55) are not listed as own methods.
results: In simulation, the RGB-only A3C policy reaches 55.30% success / 38.12 SPL on easy starts but only 1.47% on hard. Adding COCO detections hurts (36.36% easy), while trivial baselines (Random, Instant Done, Blind) are at most 7.58%. On the real LoCoBot the same policy drops to 33.33% success and 3.53 SPL on easy and 0% on hard. Even a policy overfit to the test-dev scene loses most of its SPL (82.17→12.28 easy) and half its hard-case success (94.12→50) in the real world. FOV mismatch and CycleGAN adaptation further collapse performance (16%/0% and 0%).
limitations: Benchmark experiments are very small: a single target category (Television), 2 test-dev scenes, and only a handful of real-robot episodes because runs last up to 10 minutes, so real-world percentages are coarse.
Baselines are simple reactive A3C policies with frozen ImageNet features. No mapping, depth or modern ObjectNav methods are evaluated, and no method to close the sim2real gap is proposed.
Remote-access physical testing depends on a single hosted facility; the success criterion and distance threshold are not precisely specified in the paper.
builds_on: SAVN (Wortsman et al. 2019) semantic navigation setup
